details.publicNotes:
Book beasts are shapeshifters with a relentless appetite for knowledge. Unfortunately for academics everywhere, a book beast's method of absorbing information involves literally consuming the volume. Book beasts are fond of disguising themselves as intriguing books, hoping that an unsuspecting scholar will carry them to a new library.

When a book beast eats text containing arcane formulas, they can internalize the knowledge and apply it to cast spells. While a typical book beast resonates with arcane magic, there are rumors of book beasts tied to other traditions, like esoteric tomes with occult spells or prayer books with divine spells.

Don't Judge a Book Beast by its Cover

It's rarely possible to discern a book beast's strength by their appearance. What appears to be a ratty and worn-out volume might contain the knowledge of centuries, while a shiny new tome might be a young book beast just starting out on their journey of collection.

On the other hand, young book beasts sometimes choose to replicate older books for their gravitas, while elders might decide to mimic the latest arcane treatise to catch a wizard's eye. The main difference between elder book beasts and their juniors is that elders can sometimes consume enough arcane material to develop the capacity to cast more numerous and powerful spells.

You fire a ray of heat and flame. Make a spell attack roll against a single creature. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 fire damage, and on a critical hit, the target takes double damage.

For each additional action you use when Casting the Spell, you can fire an additional ray at a different target, to a maximum of three rays targeting three different targets for 3 actions. These attacks each increase your multiple attack penalty, but you don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after you make all the spell attack rolls for blazing bolt. If you spend 2 or more actions Casting the Spell, the damage increases to 4d6 fire damage on a hit, and it still deals double damage on a critical hit.

Heightened (+1) The damage to each target increases by 1d6 for the 1-action version, or by 2d6 for the 2-action and 3-action versions.

You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

You defy gravity and levitate the target 5 feet off the ground. You can Sustain the spell to move the target up or down 10 feet. A creature floating in the air from levitate takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls. A floating creature can spend an Interact action to stabilize itself and negate this penalty for the remainder of its turn. If the target is adjacent to a fixed object or terrain of suitable stability, it can move across the surface by climbing (if the surface is vertical, like a wall) or crawling (if the surface is horizontal, such as a ceiling). The GM determines which surfaces can be climbed or crawled across.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.JqrTrvwV7pYStMXz]{Spell Effect: Levitate}

A bolt of lightning strikes outward from your hand, dealing 4d12 electricity damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12.

You learn the direction to the target (if you picked a specific object, such as "my mother's sword") or the nearest target (if you picked a type of object, such as "swords"). If the target is a specific object, you must have observed it directly with your own senses. If it's a type of object, you still need to have an accurate mental image of the type of object. If there's lead or running water between you and the target, this spell can't locate the object. This means you might find a type of object farther away if the nearest one is behind lead or running water.

Heightened (5th) You can target a specific creature or ancestry instead of an object, but you must have met or seen up close the creature or ancestry you want to target.

You create a connection between a creature's body and an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. The target's body is partially displaced toward that space, causing significant pain throughout their entire body. The target must attempt a Fortitude save. If the target fails or critically fails its save, it can choose not to be relocated, at the cost of taking double damage from the spell.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes 2d6 slashing damage.

Failure The target takes 4d6 slashing damage and is moved to the linked space.

Critical Failure The target takes 6d6 slashing damage and is moved to the linked space. Unlike most forced movement, a critical failure against agonizing relocation can move its target into a dangerous location.

Heightened (4th) Increase the slashing damage to 3d6 on a success, 6d6 on a failure, or 9d6 on a critical failure. The spell's range increases to 100 feet, and the unoccupied space chosen can be within 30 feet of the target.

Heightened (6th) Increase the slashing damage to 4d6 on a success, 8d6 on a failure, or 12d6 on a critical failure. The spell's range increases to 500 feet, and the unoccupied space chosen can be within 60 feet of the target.

The target can understand the meaning of a single language it is hearing or reading when you cast the spell. This doesn't let it understand codes, language couched in metaphor, and the like (subject to GM discretion). If the target can hear multiple languages and knows that, it can choose which language to understand; otherwise, choose one of the languages randomly.

Heightened (3rd) The target can also speak the language.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 creatures, and targets can also speak the language.

You shout a command that's hard to ignore. You can command the target to approach you, run away (as if it had the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition), release what it's holding, drop @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, or stand in place. It can't @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.A72nHGUtNXgY5Ey9]{Delay} or take any reactions until it has obeyed your command. The effects depend on the target's Will save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For the first action on its next turn, the creature must use a single action to do as you command.

Critical Failure The target must use all its actions on its next turn to obey your command.

Heightened (5th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

You snap your fingers and point at a target, which begins to smolder. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC, dealing 2d4 fire damage on a hit. If the target is within your melee reach, you can choose to make a melee spell attack with the flame instead of a ranged spell attack, which increases all the spell's damage dice to d6s.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and 1d4 persistent fire damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 1d4 and the persistent fire damage on a critical hit increases by 1d4.

description.value: The book beast changes its appearance into that of a Tiny book or reverts their appearance back to their true form. When taking the form of a book, the book beast can choose what their cover looks like as well as the text and illustrations that appear on each page. If the content includes complex diagrams or illustrations, the book beast must roll a Crafting check to determine their quality. In addition to replicating non-magical books, a book beast can take the form of a spellbook that contains all of the spontaneous spells they can cast. The book beast can't make Strikes in its Book Form.

Requirements The book beast is adjacent to an unattended book, scroll, or other written work

Effect The book beast spends 1 minute to physically devour the written work, absorbing the knowledge held within as if it had read the entire text. If the writing contains knowledge of specific arcane spells, such as a wizard's spellbook or a scroll, the book beast can freely retrain any number of their spontaneous spells into arcane spells of the same rank from the devoured source.

When a book beast successfully Grabs a creature larger than themselves with their jaws, they exude bookbinding glue from their mouth and then attach their cover to that creature. The @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} creature is not @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but if it moves, the book beast moves with it. While the book beast is attached, the book beast is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and the attached creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its saving throws against the book beast's spells. If the attached creature is Medium or smaller, it also takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.Z03EjfDZXyEzJOFQ]{Effect: Sticky Page}

Requirements The book beast is in its Book Form

Effect Until the book beast acts, they resemble an inanimate book. They have an automatic result of 30 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as a book.
